You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

The patch fixes two page pool leaks in the `lan966x_fdma` driver:

1. **`lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc()`** – After creating the page pool (`rx->page_pool`), if the subsequent `fdma_alloc_coherent()` call fails, the function now destroys the page pool before returning the error. Previously it leaked the pool.

2. **`lan966x_fdma_init()`** – If `lan966x_fdma_tx_alloc()` fails after `lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc()` has already been successfully called (and thus a page pool created), the error path now additionally calls `page_pool_destroy(lan966x->rx.page_pool)` to destroy the previously created pool. Previously only the coherent DMA memory was freed, but the page pool was left orphaned.

Both modifications address the same type of resource management bug: missing `page_pool_destroy()` in error paths that occur after the pool is allocated. The first fixes a leak within the allocation function itself; the second fixes a leak in the initialization sequence when a later allocation step fails.

content: You are a programming expert.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        In `lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc()`, after successfully creating the page pool, a failure in `fdma_alloc_coherent()` does not destroy the pool, causing a leak. In `lan966x_fdma_init()`, after `lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc()` succeeds (creating the page pool), a subsequent failure in `lan966x_fdma_tx_alloc()` only frees coherent DMA memory but omits destroying the page pool, leading to another leak. Both cases stem from missing `page_pool_destroy()` calls in error paths.
        
        Commit message:
        net: lan966x: fix page pool leak in error paths

lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc() creates a page pool but does not destroy it if
the subsequent fdma_alloc_coherent() call fails, leaking the pool.

Similarly, lan966x_fdma_init() frees the coherent DMA memory when
lan966x_fdma_tx_alloc() fails but does not destroy the page pool that
was successfully created by lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc(), leaking it.

Add the missing page_pool_destroy() calls in both error paths.

Fixes: 11871aba1974 ("net: lan96x: Use page_pool API")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: David Carlier <devnexen@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260405055241.35767-3-devnexen@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c
index 74851c63e46a..10773fe93d4d 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c
@@ -119,8 +119,10 @@ static int lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc(struct lan966x_rx *rx)
 		return PTR_ERR(rx->page_pool);
 
 	err = fdma_alloc_coherent(lan966x->dev, fdma);
-	if (err)
+	if (err) {
+		page_pool_destroy(rx->page_pool);
 		return err;
+	}
 
 	fdma_dcbs_init(fdma, FDMA_DCB_INFO_DATAL(fdma->db_size),
 		       FDMA_DCB_STATUS_INTR);
@@ -957,6 +959,7 @@ int lan966x_fdma_init(struct lan966x *lan966x)
 	err = lan966x_fdma_tx_alloc(&lan966x->tx);
 	if (err) {
 		fdma_free_coherent(lan966x->dev, &lan966x->rx.fdma);
+		page_pool_destroy(lan966x->rx.page_pool);
 		return err;
 	}
